1: Much later in the ninth century, a sharp conflict developed between Rav Saadia Gaon and Ben Meir, the Gaon of the land of Israel. The conflict was not just theoretical but practical, surrounding the designation of the time of the sanctification of the month on any given month. The conflict turned into a conflict of authority. The Gaon of the land of Israel claimed the authority over the sanctification of the months for the sages of the land of Israel and for the Sanhedrin, whereas Rav Saadia Gaon argued that the calendar was set according to the set calendar, and the eyewitness testimony was only to publicize the ceremony.24We will not get involved with the conflict over the set calendar during the time of the Geonim, as it deviates from the scope of our discussion. Though this conflict is beyond the scope of our discussion, it nevertheless has a surprising influence on some of the sources in our hands. It is likely that in the course of the debate, both sides "recruited" midrashic statements for their benefit. So in the course of the clarification [of the issue], a few sources were refined, and ancient traditions were revamped in such a way that the desired (correct) message stand out. Hence it is sometimes hard to know whether a given source was written at the time of the Amoraim or whether the version we have was revised in view of later polemical needs.
